sents.t: After I got my license, I started saving money for a car.
By April, I had five thousand dollars.
Carlos came with me to a used car lot outside town.
“Don’t buy the first car you see,” he said.
“And don’t believe everything the salesman says.”
The salesman, Rick, showed us three cars.
A red sports car was the fastest and the most beautiful, but it was too expensive, and it used a lot of gas.
A big black truck was the largest, but it had over two hundred thousand miles.
Then Rick showed us a small silver car.
It was older than the truck, but it had fewer miles, and it was the cheapest of the three: forty-eight hundred dollars.
Carlos checked the tires and looked under the hood.
We took it for a test drive.
“Can you lower the price?” Carlos asked.
“OK, forty-five hundred. That’s my best price,” Rick said.
I paid, signed the papers, and drove my own car home for the first time!
That evening, I took Rosa and Max to the lake, and we ate ice cream with the windows down.
